caption:
Did you know the Statue of Liberty's arm arrived years before the rest of her? 🗽

In 1876 only her right arm and torch had crossed the Atlantic, shown at the Centennial Exposition in Philadelphia, where visitors bought tickets to climb a ladder up to the balcony around the flame. From 1876 to 1882 the arm stood in Madison Square Park in New York, a giant advert to raise money for her pedestal. Meanwhile her head went on show at the 1878 world's fair in Paris while workers built the rest. When the pedestal fund ran dry, Joseph Pulitzer promised to print the name of every donor in his newspaper, the World. Roughly 125,000 people gave, most about a dollar or less, and she was unveiled in New York Harbor on 28 October 1886.
